featured_reviews.name: Harish
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Grey Soul Coffee Roasters in Bandra to explore their pour-over program, and it’s clear the café is serious about specialty coffee. The menu is thoughtfully structured, with detailed coffee cards covering estate, varietal, altitude, and processing.

I tried the “Raspberry in Loop” from Zoya Estate (Chikmagalur), a light roast featuring S795 and Chandragiri varietals processed through multi-stage anaerobic fermentation. On paper, this is a high-potential coffee designed for a fruit-forward, layered profile.

In the cup, however, the experience didn’t fully align with expectations. While the coffee was clean and free of defects, the flavor expression felt muted — the brighter fruit notes (pineapple, mandarin, raspberry) and deeper chocolate tones were not clearly defined. The cup leaned more toward a subdued, flattened profile rather than the vibrant complexity suggested by the processing.

The barista interaction was informative and helpful, and the overall setup reflects a strong intent toward quality and transparency.

Grey Soul is still worth visiting for those interested in Indian specialty coffee and experimental processing. However, in this instance, the brewing didn’t fully unlock the potential of an otherwise very interesting coffee.

featured_reviews.review_text:
you're ever around Pali Hill, Bandra West, and looking for a cozy, aesthetic spot to chill with friends or even get some work done, Ritual Daily Coffee should definitely be on your list. This café is not only known for its specialty coffee but also for its calm ambience, comfortable seating, and work-friendly vibe.

We tried their Iced Vanilla Latte, and it was as good as it looked — smooth, refreshing, and perfectly balanced in flavor. My friend went for the Biscoff Frappe, and honestly, it was a game-changer. The taste was unique and indulgent, with that Biscoff twist hitting all the right notes.

Now, let's talk food — we ordered their Rose Chicken Croffle Sandwich, and wow, this was mind-blowing. The flavor, the creativity, the texture — everything about it stood out. I can confidently say you won’t find a sandwich like this anywhere else in Mumbai. My friend and I both absolutely loved it.

We also tried the Chicken Club Sandwich, and it was packed with juicy chicken and fresh vegetables — hearty, flavorful, and satisfying. The Chicken Cilantro Quesadillas were another highlight, highly recommended by the staff, and they didn’t disappoint.

The cherry on top? Their Mango Basque Cheesecake. Soft, rich, and just the right amount of sweet — it was the perfect way to end our meal.

Service was excellent, with the staff being super friendly and helpful in recommending their best dishes. The overall experience was a solid 10/10.

Whether you're looking for a new coffee hangout, a place to work, or just craving some standout food, Ritual Daily Coffee is definitely worth the visit.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Rajpal
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a warm and cozy café in Bandra West, Rituals Café is such a lovely find! From the moment you walk in, the vibe feels inviting – it has that cute, aesthetic charm that makes you want to sit down, relax, and just spend hours there. The upper deck seating is one of my favorite parts – perfect for catching up with friends, getting some work done, or even just enjoying a quiet coffee by yourself.

Coming to the food – I tried their mac & cheese and it was exactly what comfort food should taste like: creamy, cheesy, and super satisfying. The avo toast with burrata was fresh and delicious, such a perfect combination. For dessert, I went with their gluten-free chocolate cake and honestly, I couldn’t believe it was gluten-free – it was rich, fudgy, and just the right amount of sweetness. I also loved their 54% sugar-free Belgian chocolate – guilt-free but still indulgent. To finish, I had the Brazilian blueberry smoothie, which was refreshing, light, and packed with flavor.

What I really like is that everything feels thoughtfully made, and the presentation is just as good as the taste. It’s not just a café, but a spot where you can actually unwind and feel good while enjoying great food. Definitely one of those hidden gems in Bandra that I’ll be revisiting for sure. Highly recommend to anyone who loves cozy corners, comfort food, and cute café vibes! 💛

Consistency would make a big difference here.

featured_reviews.name: Niyati Singhvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re tired of the long wait times at Boojee Cafe, walk a few metres over to Bokka Coffee.
Honestly, the quality is just as competitive without the headache. We were a group of two and got seated immediately (luckily enough). The staff was incredibly responsive and attentive to us. I highly recommend the chocolate bowl if you want something indulgent, and the hibiscus iced tea is perfect for something refreshing.
It’s not "cheap," but it certainly won't burn a hole in your pocket—it’s priced just right for the experience.
Plus, the plant-filled, well-lit decor makes for a great atmosphere.
Definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Suhel Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Heard this is one of Shahid Kapoor’s favorite coffee spots, so decided to drop by and give it a try. Located in the busy lanes of Khar, the café thankfully offers valet parking, which is a big plus.

The space is cozy but quite compact, so some wait time is expected during rush hours. Seating can feel a bit close together, and note that laptops or tablets aren’t allowed, so it’s not a spot to work from. The ambiance is warm and inviting, filled with plants and soft lighting that adds to the charm.

Service was excellent — staff were attentive and quick to respond. Tried the iced Americano, which had a nice balance of flavor without being overly bitter. The Harvest Salad with salmon was fresh and generous in portion, and the Berry Bowl was naturally sweet with no added sugar.

Pricing is on par with other popular cafés in the area.
Overall, a great spot for coffee lovers and relaxed brunches, but not ideal if you’re looking to work.

featured_reviews.name: Pakshal Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bokka is a nice option to try amongst the hundreds of other within the collection of cafes in Bandra

We ordered their Strawberry Matcha Oatie and Iced Mocha. Both were solid options (8.5/10) but I was left wanting for more after having their Matcha

Would definitely visit again to try their food offerings

featured_reviews.name: Raseel Bhagat
featured_reviews.review_text: The place was too congested for my comfort. And even though they have a wide range of a healthy menu, the taste was mid at best. The coffees were really good though.

featured_reviews.name: Safa Chhabdia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bokka serves one of the best coffee’s in bandra.
Love their Vietnamese iced latte.
They also offer great options in food & healthy desserts.
The shroom sandwich , pesto dosa and cakes are a must try.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Sancheti
featured_reviews.review_text: It's a cozy cafe with fancy and aromatic coffee options. Food is delicious specially the avocado toast, Dosa and chia bowl which we like to have. Nice place to sit and talk. I would recommend for a group of 2-4 max. Good place to check out for coffee.

featured_reviews.name: Sahil Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually go for the regular cold brew, but this time I tried the Citrus Cold Brew (unsweetened) , that version didn’t quite hit the mark for me. However, the staff was super kind and offered to remake it, and the second one tasted much better. Really appreciate the gesture and their customer-first attitude!

We also tried the Croissant Chicken Sandwich, which was absolutely delicious, buttery, flaky, and perfectly balanced and the Korean Potatoes, which had that tangy, addictive flavor you can’t stop eating.

Overall, a cozy spot with great service and food that stands out. Definitely coming back for more!

featured_reviews.review_text: My wife and I went to their cafe in Bandra in the start of 2025 and I instantly fell in love with the place. featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stumbled upon a hidden gem in Bandra completely by accident—and honestly, that made it even better.

We were actually on our way to a different coffee spot, took a wrong turn, hit a dead end… and found this place instead. No plans, no expectations—just pure luck.

We ordered a Hot Bombon and a VM House Phin Coffee, and both were absolutely amazing. The bombon especially stood out—this is probably the first time I genuinely enjoyed a sweet hot coffee without feeling like it was too much. It just hit perfectly.

For food, we tried the Chicken & Avocado Sandwich. Taste-wise, it was really good, but I felt like the avocado got a bit lost under the mayo. Maybe something like adding the chicken into a guacamole-style mix could balance the flavors better—just a small suggestion.

The ambience? Spot on. Aesthetic, cozy, and exactly what you’d want from a coffee place where you can just sit, relax, and enjoy the moment.

Safe to say, sometimes getting lost leads you to better places than you planned. 🌿☕

featured_reviews.name: Eshwar Reddy
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is an absolute gem of a café! Super cozy vibes, one of the best prawn rolls I’ve ever had, and the avocado chicken sandwich was insanely good.

Perfect spot for your next brunch outing.

The staff were incredibly warm and respectful, and the barista was genuinely lovely too. Definitely a café worth coming back to!

featured_reviews.name: Smita Vyas Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanilla Miel is tough to find as it is tucked away inside Pali village with very little signage to guide you to it. But that is about the only grouse I have. The place is beautiful and minimal. The service is courteous and the winner is the food.

This is the first time in a very very long time that a restuarant actually made scrambled eggs as they are supposed to be: moist and soft. And the French toast ohh lala! C'est magnifique. I would have licked the plate if I was not as well-behaved as my mother taught me to be;)

Between 3 of us we ordered 5 dishes and 3 drinks and spent 3600 which was quite reasonable i  thought.

I will definitely be going again.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. CHAITANYA JASTI
featured_reviews.review_text: A place which one would love to visit again. Located in the heart of Pali Village, this place offers you a true Goan/Portugese vibe. This place offers the mind calmimg view of pali village and one can enjoy the soul of it to the core. We tried the lamb and chicken dishes for breakfast and both were top notch. I loved the Flat White from their espresso bar.

featured_reviews.name: Vandana
featured_reviews.review_text: A must go! Quaint lane of Pali Village. Super cool vintage Vibe. Loved the white n wood combo of the decor. Enjoyed a peaceful evening with the family. Coffee was well brewed, Textures of mushroom tart recommended by the server was nice. Cajun strawberry chick sandwich was yummm… just found the kimchi flavour in Kimchi cheese toastiest a bit mild… the cheese dominated the taste… but all in all a Lovely experience… 👍🏼✅

featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Sharma

Coffee was great, chai was too overcooked (bitter )

Rest the coffee was good too and the staff was super polite.

featured_reviews.name: Megha Ghosh

Food is great. I prefer the Linguine Pasta and the Pancakes here.

featured_reviews.name: Diana Goveas
featured_reviews.review_text:
They have locations in Worli and Bandra West, and people seem to enjoy their menu
- *Kejriwal Multigrain Dosa* was the best and a must have, sunny side up egg on multigrain dosa with cheese and their in house mint chutney is spot on.
- *Kimchi Scrambled Eggs* popular Korean-inspired breakfast option, made with scrambled eggs, kimchi, and served with toast. The spicy kick from the kimchi pairs well with the creamy eggs.
- *Tiramisu dessert served in a coffee cup*: A creative twist on the classic Italian dessert! coffee-infused dessert made with ladyfingers, mascarpone cheese, and cocoa powder.

-Friendly staff,  quick service however it’s packed on weekends so service is delayed.

featured_reviews.name: Suhel Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited this outlet after seeing a few posts floating around instagram.
The place offers both outdoor and indoor seating and is pet friendly. Found the seating space to be a little tight, tables too close to each other.
Ordered a sea salt mocha listed under house special and it lived up to its listing. Perfect balance between the coffee and dark chocolate. No additional sweetner required.
For food, ordered a Souvlaki, a well plated mix of a healthy balanced meal.
Pricing is at par compared to other well known outlets and justifues the quality.
The staff were very warm and welcoming. Service was on point. Got the coffee re-heated. Valet parking is available.
Great spot for good quality coffee and healthy food.

featured_reviews.name: Rachna Chirania
featured_reviews.review_text: Loved my experience at Standby Coffee, Bandra! The coffee is rich and perfectly brewed — I tried the cold filter coffee, it was made to perfection. The space has a calm, minimal vibe which is great for hanging out. Friendly staff, quick service, and quality beans make this café a must-visit for any coffee lover in Bandra. They offer all the healthy food options which is really tasty.

featured_reviews.name: Ankur Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving indulgent hot or cold chocolate in Mumbai, Chantilly and Chantilly Works, Bandra is an absolute must-visit.

They serve one of the best strawberry chocolates and hot/cold chocolates the city has to offer. It’s clearly a favorite among many—and honestly, I completely get why.

Yes, it may seem a bit pricey at first, but the quality and experience make it totally worth it. I’d highly recommend trying their 75% dark chocolate version—rich, intense, and perfectly balanced.

A little personal ritual I swear by:
I usually order a hot chocolate, enjoy half there, and take the rest home. Refrigerate it overnight and have it cold the next day—it tastes incredible!

One thing to note: the seating space is very small—just a few tables. If you visit at night, be prepared for a wait, even for takeaway sometimes.

I’m not even a big chocolate person, but this place is an exception I happily make.

Must visit when your chocolate cravings hit! 🍫

featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to this spot on Saturday morning for breakfast, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience for us.

We ordered one Cortado, a large Pain au Chocolat, a spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown, an avocado chicken sandwich, and a Caramel Latte.

The cortado was incredible; it's a traditional Spanish espresso drink made with double espresso and 60 ml of milk. It had a bitter flavour, but I really enjoyed it.

The large pain au chocolat was absolutely delicious, a classic pastry crafted from buttery, flaky, laminated dough (similar to croissant dough) wrapped around dark chocolate sticks.

The spicy chicken-stuffed hash brown was tasty, featuring shredded potatoes filled with cooked chicken, pan-fried until golden and crispy.The avocado chicken sandwich was mouthwatering and highly recommended. It was a fresh, nutritious, and versatile meal made with thin slices of chicken and avocado. Simply delightful.

The caramel latte was incredibly refreshing. It’s a sweet and creamy coffee drink typically made with espresso, steamed milk, and caramel syrup.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Absolutely loved how this cafe is designed-it may look small from the outside, but the interiors are planned so well that it feels surprisingly spacious and comfortable once you step in. It’s a perfect spot for a quick bite with friends or even a casual catch-up over coffee.

The place gets quite packed on weekends. We went on a Saturday and had to wait around 5–10 minutes for a table, which honestly just shows how popular the cafe is.

The food and coffee here are fantastic. The House Cold Coffee was suggested to us and it truly lived up to the hype, a must-try if you’re a genuine coffee lover. We also tried the Orange Cold Brew. Personally, I didn’t enjoy it as much, but it definitely feels like an acquired taste, so cold brew enthusiasts should still give it a shot.

For food, we tried the Chicken & Veggies Mini Wrap and it was amazing, especially the dip served alongside it which paired perfectly with the wrap.

Another big plus point was the staff and service. The staff is friendly, welcoming and the service is impressively quick despite the crowd.

Overall, a really nice cafe with great vibes, good food and excellent coffee. Would definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in and around Bandra.

Eddie’s Cafe : A Culinary Joyride Through Iftaar Specials

Eddie’s Bistro has long been on my radar, and I finally decided to give their Iftaar menu a whirl, expecting nothing less than a feast for the senses. Right from the get-go, the presentation scored high marks; the food arrived in pristine packaging that promised good things within.

featured_reviews.name: Supreet Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Eddie's Bistro on a rainy Saturday evening few months back. Eddie's is nicely tucked away amongst a plethora of stores and restaurants on Pali Hill, and can actually be difficult to spot. Once inside though, the place is actually pretty large and has an outdoor seating area as well (preferred by the smokers). The place was packed as expected by revellers, and we had to wait about 15 minutes to get a table, which we had to switch thrice because we were a group of 7 and the first two tables were uncomfortable. Finally, two tables were conjoined to our comfort. The ambience is nice with a orangish feel and nice decor.

Coming to the main part, which are the food and beverages. I decided to go for a New York Sour, while my friends were in the mood for some beer. They ordered some Bira's, followed by a bucket of Corona's.

For starters, we ordered Stuffed Chicken Roulade's and Greek Chicken Kebab's. The Roulade's were good, slightly on the sour side, with some delicious sauce. The Kebab's came on mini-skewers, dipped with a yogurt sauce, always a good combination with chicken if you ask me.

In our next round, we ordered Grilled chicken, which came with sides of mashed potato and roasted veggies. The chicken was well-cooked, and the quantity was pretty good, to say the least. Next came the Bechamel Sauce Chicken Pasta, and the Tomato Sauce Chicken Pasta. I am not the biggest fan of tomato sauce, but I liked the Bechamel Sauce pasta, with generous chunks of chicken and a pair of garlic bread to go with it.

We ended the night with mini lamb sliders and some lime chilli squid. I am a big fan of squid, and the tangy taste of the lime chilli made it a wonderful concoction. To be honest, I was unimpressed by the sliders though.

Overall, the place gets 4 from me, service was a bit slow on the night, but polite and courteous. Music was too loud at times, and it was difficult to have a conversation, but then again, this place maybe isn't one to have a conversation at. I felt the prices were overall reasonable.

The menu can definitely do with some more options, I would recommend it to anyone on the lookout for some nice food and drinks.

featured_reviews.name: Ankan Singhal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and came away with mixed feelings.

We ordered the Mushroom Sandwich on sourdough, Paneer Tikka Panini, Pink Sauce Pasta, Veg Burger with fries, Cold Chocolate, and ended the meal with a Chocolate Cake.

Starting with the sandwiches, the Mushroom Sandwich was unfortunately quite dry and lacked the moisture and flavour you would expect. The Paneer Tikka Panini had the opposite problem, the mustard was so overpowering that it completely dominated the dish, making it taste more like a mustard sandwich than a paneer tikka panini.

The Pink Sauce Pasta was decent but nothing memorable. It wasn't bad, but it didn't stand out either.

The Veg Burger was actually the star of the meal. It was well-made, flavourful, and easily the best savoury dish we ordered. However, what left a sour taste was being charged ₹50 extra to make just a handful of fries peri-peri. Charging that amount for a full portion is understandable, but for barely six fries on the side, it felt excessive and unnecessary.

The Cold Chocolate was another disappointment—not because of the taste, which was perfectly fine, but because of the quantity. The portion felt quite small for the price being charged.

Thankfully, dessert ended the meal on a positive note. The Chocolate Cake was rich, delicious, and probably the highlight of the entire experience.

Overall, August Café has a pleasant atmosphere and some good offerings, but the food lacked consistency and some of the pricing decisions felt difficult to justify. Not a bad experience, but not one that left a strong impression either.

⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)

featured_reviews.name: Adriel Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and had quite a mixed but overall pleasant experience.

Starting with the Pho, this unfortunately missed the mark. It wasn’t authentic, used the wrong type of noodles, and the balance of flavours was overwhelmed by an excess of chilli oil and flakes. The Soy Chilli Noodles were also underwhelming; they lacked depth and flavour, and didn’t really stand out as a noodle dish.

On the brighter side, the Nachos were, as always, spot on, crisp, generously topped, and satisfying. The Chicken Steak with Peri Peri Sauce was another highlight, perfectly cooked, tender, and flavourful, paired beautifully with fresh, well-seasoned vegetables.

For drinks, the Elderberry Fizz with soda and basil seeds was refreshing and unique, while the Cappuccino was smooth and well-prepared.

Desserts were a strong finish to the meal; there’s a great variety to choose from. The Tiramisu Waffle was indulgent without being overly sweet, and the Ice Cream Sundae with a brownie base, ice cream, and caramel sauce was rich and satisfying.

The service deserves special mention, the staff are exceptionally polite, attentive, and quick. There’s an air-conditioned indoor section for comfort, as well as outdoor seating with a smoking area for those who prefer al fresco dining.

Not every dish hit the right note, but the warm service and pleasant ambience stood out. That said, for the meal we had and the overall experience, the pricing felt steep. While the service and setting are commendable, some dishes need refinement for the cost to feel justified.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Affogato – a must-visit coffee and gelato outlet located on 17th Road in Khar West, Mumbai (near Bandra).
It looks tiny and unassuming from the roadside, but once you step inside, the stunning interior and inviting aroma of fresh coffee and gelato welcome you. The space feels like it was carved out of a smooth, swirling rock or cave — with soft curves, textured beige micro-concrete walls, ceiling, and floors inspired by gelato swirls. It's truly magical and artistic!
They offer two seating options: outdoor (without AC) and a cozy indoor AC room. The menu has a great variety of cakes, pastries, coffees, and, of course, their signature affogatos (espresso over gelato).
I tried their Cappuccino and Pain au Chocolat — both were excellent! The cappuccino came in a stylish glass cup, and the croissant was flaky, buttery, and perfectly chocolate-filled. Service was friendly and attentive.
One small downside: there's no strong AC blower at the entrance, so a few mosquitoes can be a minor nuisance (typical Mumbai evening issue in humid weather).
Overall, the experience was fantastic — highly recommended for any coffee or gelato lover in the city! ☕🍦✨

Seating is available both indoors and outdoors — though slightly limited and snug. I tried the avocado chicken, which came in a generous portion for the price and delivered beautifully on flavor. They also serve excellent gelatos, including sugar-free options sweetened with monk fruit — a thoughtful touch. Definitely planning to return to try those and the tempting quiche next time!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Affogato in Khar for the first time and I must say it was an absolute delight. I ordered the hazelnut affogato and it was heavenly. The blend of rich espresso poured over the creamy hazelnut gelato created the perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness. The café itself has a very chic and calming vibe. It’s minimal in its design yet incredibly warm and welcoming. The use of earthy tones and the cozy setting give it a very homely feel. It’s the kind of place that instantly puts you at ease and makes you want to stay a little longer.

A big shoutout to Amit from the staff. He was genuinely sweet and courteous. We happened to be the last ones to place our order and despite the system being shut, when we expressed interest in trying the coffee gelato, Amit went out of his way to let us sample it in a small container. featured_reviews.review_text:
As a coffee and dessert enthusiast, discovering Affogato x Coffee by Javaphile was a delightful experience. This café offers a unique blend of Italian-inspired gelato and artisanal coffee, making it a must-visit for anyone who enjoys high-quality coffee and desserts.

Ambience & Design

The moment I walked in, I was captivated by the café's minimalist and modern design. The interiors have a soft, monochromatic palette inspired by swirling gelato, creating a serene and inviting atmosphere. The large, curved glass windows let in plenty of natural light, making it a perfect spot to unwind with a coffee. The outdoor seating area, surrounded by lush greenery and a calming white gravel setting, adds to the charm, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a peaceful break.

Menu Highlights

As the name suggests, Affogato x Coffee specializes in affogatos, and I couldn’t resist trying their signature affogato with Belgian Chocolate gelato. The combination of hot espresso and cold, velvety gelato was nothing short of amazing! They also have a great selection of gelato flavors, from Salted Butter Caramel to Tiramisu, all crafted using traditional Italian methods.

For those looking for something beyond affogatos, the café also offers freshly baked goods like Almond Croissants, Pain au Chocolat, and Cinnamon Rolls, which pair beautifully with their coffee. If you’re into unique coffee flavors, I highly recommend their Sea Salt Mocha or Spiced Latte—both have a perfect balance of richness and depth.

Service & Atmosphere

The staff here is friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about coffee and gelato. They are happy to guide you through the menu and help you find the perfect pairing. Another great thing is that this café is pet-friendly, making it a fantastic spot for those who want to enjoy their coffee with their furry friends.

Final Thoughts

Affogato x Coffee by Javaphile beautifully blends the art of gelato-making with specialty coffee, creating a haven for both dessert and coffee lovers. Whether you're craving a classic affogato, a scoop of creamy gelato, or a freshly brewed coffee, this place promises a memorable experience.

Would I visit again? Without a doubt!
